Log the calls to an asynchronous function

Source: R/async_log_call.R
async_log_call.Rd

Asynchronous version of log_call(), for functions that return a promise. It logs the start when the function is called, and the finish or the failure when the promise settles, with the time taken up to that point. A rejection is logged then passed on unchanged. Needs the promises package.

Usage

async_log_call(f, logger = logger_base(), level = log_levels(), elapsed = TRUE)

Arguments

f

The function to decorate. Usually supplied by %@% rather than directly.

logger

A logger, such as logger_message(). See extending_log to use a logging package.

level

A log_levels() giving the level of the start, finish and error events.

elapsed

Include the time taken in the finish and error messages?

Value

A decorator. The decorated function returns a promise.

Details

There is no trace argument, as the calls that led to a rejection are no longer on the stack by the time it settles.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
fn := async_log_call(logger = logger_message()) %@%
  function(x) promises::promise_resolve(x)
promises::then(fn(1), print)
while (!later::loop_empty()) later::run_now(0.05)
} # }
